News global nation business lifestyle entertainment technology sports opinion LATEST NEWS STORIES HEADLINES METRO REGIONS NATION WORLD CDN NEWSLETTER www / Philippine Elections Philippine Elections Comelec reminds public: No fees for voter certifications By: Chelsy Claire Perez - @inquirerdotnet INQUIRER.net / 05:56 PM November 19, 2026 Share: MANILA, Philippines – The Commission on Elections (Comelec) on Thursday reminded the public that voter certifications are issued free of charge nationwide amid reports of social media posts falsely claiming that applicants were being charged for the document.
Comelec Chair George Erwin Garcia said the certification is free regardless of the number of copies requested or whether it is obtained from the commission’s main office or any of its field offices.
“Comelec gives all voter certifications for free in the whole Philippines, whether it is here in the main office or in the field, there is no fee,” Garcia said.
He cited reports circulating in Sultan Kudarat province alleging that applicants were being asked to pay P20 for each voter certification. However, Garcia said the commission’s verification found that the post came from a fake account.
“We verified, we counter-checked; it turns out that it is a fake account. So there are people like that,” he said.

The Comelec had earlier reiterated that voter certifications have been issued free of charge since 2022 as part of its efforts to “streamline frontline registration services.”
Separately, the Comelec Region XII office also addressed a social media post alleging that a voter was charged P20 for a certification at the Comelec office in Matalam, North Cotabato.
In a statement posted on social media, the regional office stressed that voter certifications are free and warned against unauthorized fee collection.
“We wish to emphasize that the issuance of Voter Certification is FREE OF CHARGE under existing COMELEC rules. We will not tolerate any unauthorized collection of fees,” it said.
READ: Comelec opens voter registration for 2028 polls from Nov. 10 to July 30
The regional office said it had launched an investigation and was reaching out to the owner of the social media account to obtain her account of the incident and any available evidence.
It also denied an allegation that its office had referred to the complainant as “reklamador.”
“For the record, no such communication has been made by our Office, nor has any such remark been uttered by us,” it said.
The regional office said it was taking the matter seriously and remained committed to upholding accountability, professionalism and integrity in its services.
